title: A world record run alone, and the interference effect that didn't show up
summary: Agnes Ngetich's 1:05:15 women-only world record in Copenhagen and what her 5 km splits say about solo pacing; a PLOS One paper finding the lactate minimum test does not produce a true lactate steady state; the Sports Medicine umbrella review of 17 meta-analyses on concurrent training; and whether advanced lifting techniques beat straight sets once volume and effort are matched.
